core_meaning.primary_meaning: Sadat corresponds to the Arabic form سَادَات and is glossed in this record as “Lords, masters.” The record associates the form with root س و د (s-w-d). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Sadat corresponds to the Arabic form سَادَات (Arabic root س و د (s-w-d); سَادَات (Sādāt)). Its core sense is sadat; lords, masters (plural). Sadat is Arabic سَادَات (Sādāt) 'lords, masters', the plural of سَيِّد (sayyid). CRITICAL SOURCE ERROR: the source gave صادَت (a non-standard form). The source gloss 'Ruler, Lady' is broadly consistent.

persian.name: سادات
